summary: MISO and its transmission owners file tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in a new docket, ER27-526-000. The filing adds a Large Load Project Review with a $250,000 application fee, two pro forma cost recovery agreements, a public dashboard, and two new services, Firm Service Step Up and Interim NITS.
ask: Accept the revisions effective February 14, 2027, 90 days after filing, with a 30-day comment period.

points.point: MISO says this filing, the companion GRITS filing and its pending large-load filings together answer FERC's concerns.
points.quote: MISO’s other pending Large Load filings fully addresses the concerns identified by the Commission

points.point: It builds on earlier filings already pending: zero-injection agreements, reliability requirements and the resource study.
points.quote: MISO has already filed several proposals responsive to the Show Cause Order that are currently pending before the Commission

points.point: A new Large Load Project Review would study every large-load service request, with deposits and milestones to deter speculative ones.
points.quote: The LLPR also includes deposits, project milestones, and other safeguards designed to discourage speculative Large Load requests.

points.point: Large-load customers would bear the cost of the upgrades built for them through cost recovery agreements.
points.quote: designed to ensure that the costs incurred to provide Transmission Service to Large Load Transmission Customers, including the costs of Large Load Upgrades (defined herein), are born by such customers

points.point: MISO would publish the location and estimated costs of large loads on a dashboard.
points.quote: The results of the LLPR periodically will be published to provide transparency into the location and estimated costs associated with Large Load facilities in the MISO region

points.point: Two new services, Firm Service Step Up and Interim NITS, would let customers take service in stages as they build out.
points.quote: The new Transmission Services available to Large Loads include Firm Service Step Up and Interim Non-Firm NITS service.

points.point: Loads of 200 MW or more partnered with a generator for at least 15 years go through the resource study instead.
points.quote: If the Large Load is greater than or equal to 200 MW and has formally partnered with a generator for a minimum of fifteen years, then the applicants will go through the LARS study process.

points.point: MISO says states and stakeholders did not agree on everything.
points.quote: While full alignment was not achieved on every aspect of the proposals

points.point: MISO asks for a February 14, 2027 effective date and a 30-day comment period.
points.quote: MISO requests that the Commission accept the proposed revisions effective 90 days from the date of this filing (i.e., February 14, 2027).

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 by MISO and its transmission owners to answer the E-8 show cause order for MISO, alongside the companion GRITS filing and MISO's earlier large-load filings.
